name: Mass estimator: mass ladder for prior-width and sequential-update analyses

aims: Measure how a declared log-normal prior on mass changes point success when its centre is wrong by a stated factor, for several stated widths.
Measure the behaviour of three declared rules for combining independent readings of one mass (symmetric, contribution 11 eq. (18), eq. (20)), including readings with true zero excitation.
data_generating_mechanisms: Newton II is assumed correct. One compatible latent 3D pair per replicate; common direction is used only by the simulator and remains unknown to inference.

Known independent isotropic Gaussian coordinate SD 1 in both channels, one effective reading per channel, R=10000 replicates per cell with fresh seeds. The same replicate-index noise is shared across cells; cells cannot be pooled as independent evidence.

Mass and excitation independent: masses [0.25,1,4] (in units of sigma_F/sigma_a) crossed with acceleration SNR [0,1,2,3,4,6]; force SNR is mass times acceleration SNR. Zero excitation gives true zero vectors, whose observations cannot depend on mass.
estimands: Prior analysis: per cell with positive excitation and K in {1.25,1.5,2}, success change relative to the unweighted law.

Sequential analysis: consecutive series of 50 replicates of one cell treated as 50 independent readings of one mass, each with its own latent excitation; per rule and prefix N in {1,2,5,10,20,50}: readout and median relative to truth, 95% and 80% central-interval coverage, interval width. For zero excitation: location and width relative to the noise ratio.
methods: Existing isotropic comparison engine unchanged, saving all trials.
prior_weight_study.py (log-normal grids centred at a stated multiple of each cell's true mass) and sequential_update.py compute the analyses afterwards.
performance_measures: Coverage MCSE sqrt(c(1-c)/200) over 200 series per cell; success MCSE at most 0.005. Series within one cell share the cell's excitation magnitude; cells share replicate-index noise.

methodology.title: Morris, White and Crowther: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
Gneiting: Making and Evaluating Point Forecasts

interpretation: The oracle centring of the prior at a multiple of the true mass is an analysis device for pricing a wrong prior, not an estimator.
A series of 50 replicates models repeated independent experiments on one object with equal excitation magnitude; it does not model shared calibration or changing excitation.
